root_cause.text: The RISC-V IOMMU driver failed to issue mandatory IOTINVAL commands after updating Device Directory Table (DDT) or Page Directory Table (PDT) entries, violating the RISC-V IOMMU specification requirements for TLB and context cache invalidation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a new function `riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval()` that performs required TLB and context cache invalidations as mandated by RISC-V IOMMU specification Sections 6.3.1 and 6.3.2. The patch inserts calls to this function immediately after DDT/PDT entry updates in `riscv_iommu_iodir_update()` (at two locations where `riscv_iommu_cmd_send()` is called for DDT invalidation commands). Without these IOTINVAL commands, stale TLB and context cache entries could persist after DDT/PDT modifications, potentially causing incorrect address translations or device access control violations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Implement RISC-V IOMMU specification-compliant IOTINVAL command generation for DDT/PDT entry invalidation to ensure proper TLB coherency.
intent_record.what: Added a new static function `riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval()` with 67 lines of code that constructs and sends IOTINVAL commands to the RISC-V IOMMU device. The function handles different invalidation scenarios based on IOHGATP mode (bare vs. non-bare) and PDT invalidation flags, conditionally setting PSCID and GSCID fields in the command structure before transmission.
intent_record.how: This function implements the RISC-V IOMMU specification requirements (Section 6.3.1 and 6.3.2) for sending IOTINVAL commands after DDT or PDT entry modifications. It enables proper TLB invalidation by examining device configuration (IOHGATP mode, PDTV flag, FSC mode) and constructing appropriate invalidation commands with correct PSCID/GSCID parameters. The function will be called during page table updates to ensure hardware cache coherency.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing IOMMU TLB invalidation call after I/O directory updates with default parameters pending SVA/PASID feature implementation.
intent_record.what: Added a function call to riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval() with parameters (iommu, false, dc->iohgatp, dc, NULL) and a preceding multi-line comment explaining that SVA and PASID features are not yet merged and default configuration values are used.
intent_record.how: This change adds an additional IOMMU invalidation operation (iotinval) after the existing iodir command is sent. The function is called with hardcoded defaults (inval_pdt=false, pc=NULL) as a placeholder until SVA (Shared Virtual Addressing) and PASID (Process Address Space ID) features are implemented. This ensures proper TLB/cache invalidation for the I/O directory updates.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing I/O TLB invalidation call after IODIR updates to ensure TLB coherency with default parameters pending SVA/PASID feature integration.
intent_record.what: Added a function call to `riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval()` with parameters (iommu, false, dc->iohgatp, dc, NULL) after the existing `riscv_iommu_cmd_send()` call, along with a multi-line comment explaining that SVA and PASID features are not yet merged and default configuration is used.
intent_record.how: This change adds an I/O TLB invalidation operation to the IODIR update sequence. The function is called with hardcoded default parameters (inval_pdt=false, pc=NULL) to invalidate I/O TLB entries after updating the device directory entry. This ensures TLB coherency following the directory modification, though with simplified defaults pending future feature integration.

consistency_review.core_intent: Implement I/O TLB invalidation mechanisms to ensure TLB coherency following IOMMU directory updates in compliance with RISC-V IOMMU specification.

relevance_review.reason: This group directly addresses the root cause by implementing IOTINVAL command generation for DDT/PDT entry invalidation and adding missing I/O TLB invalidation calls after directory updates. These changes ensure compliance with RISC-V IOMMU specification requirements for mandatory TLB and context cache invalidation following directory table modifications.

The group directly addresses the root cause by adding the missing IOTINVAL command after I/O directory (DDT/PDT) updates. This implements the mandatory TLB invalidation required by the RISC-V IOMMU specification that was absent in the vulnerable code.

candidates.rationale: After sending IODIR invalidation commands (line 1033), the code fails to issue the mandatory IOTINVAL command to invalidate TLB/context cache entries. The specification requires IOTINVAL to follow DDT/PDT updates, but this is missing before the sync operation.

Similar to Hunk 1, after sending IODIR invalidation commands (line 1058), the mandatory IOTINVAL command is not issued before the sync operation, violating RISC-V IOMMU specification requirements for TLB coherency after DDT/PDT updates.

The code sets sync_required flag but never issues the required IOTINVAL command before synchronization. The missing IOTINVAL command between DDT/PDT updates and sync violates the specification's mandatory invalidation sequence.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement at line 1034 sets the sync_required flag but fails to issue the mandatory IOTINVAL command after DDT/PDT updates. The code violates the RISC-V IOMMU specification by not invalidating TLB/context cache entries before synchronization. The missing IOTINVAL command between the IODIR update (line 1033) and the sync operation creates a window where stale TLB entries remain cached, potentially allowing unauthorized I/O access.

This statement at line 1058 sends an IODIR invalidation command but is not followed by the mandatory IOTINVAL command required by the RISC-V IOMMU specification. After updating DDT/PDT entries via IODIR commands, the specification mandates that IOTINVAL commands must be issued to invalidate TLB and context cache entries before the sync operation. The absence of this required IOTINVAL command violates the specification's invalidation sequence requirements.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 488ffbf181718b9ad8c1838cb249d60973e78eda
Author: Tomasz Jeznach <tomasz.jeznach@linux.dev>
Date:   Tue Oct 15 23:52:19 2024 -0700

    iommu/riscv: Paging domain support
    
    Introduce first-stage address translation support.
    
    Page table configured by the IOMMU driver will use the highest mode
    implemented by the hardware, unless not known at the domain allocation
    time falling back to the CPU’s MMU page mode.
    
    This change introduces IOTINVAL.VMA command, require
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces paging domain support with proper IOTINVAL command handling. The code explicitly implements mandatory invalidation commands after DDT/PDT updates: (1) In riscv_iommu_iodir_update(), IOTINVAL.DDT commands are issued after clearing DC_TC_V (lines 1018-1021) and after updating device context (lines 1048-1051), followed by riscv_iommu_cmd_sync() at line 1053. (2) In riscv_iommu_iotlb_inval(), IOTINVAL.VMA commands are properly issued for each IOMMU linked to the protection domain (lines 969-981), with corresponding sync operations (lines 983-990). (3) In riscv_iommu_map_pages(), when freeing old page table entries, riscv_iommu_iotlb_inval() is called to invalidate cached entries (line 1180). (4) In riscv_iommu_bond_unlink(), IOTINVAL.VMA with PSCID is issued when unlinking the last device (lines 903-906). The commit message explicitly states 'This change introduces IOTINVAL.VMA command, required to invalidate any cached IOATC entries after mapping is updated and/or removed from the paging domain.' All mandatory invalidation sequences are present and properly synchronized with IOFENCE commands.
